memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Joseph said to his brothers and to his father's household, 'I will go up and speak to Pharaoh and will say to him, "My brothers and my father's household, who were living in the land of Canaan, have come to me. The men are shepherds; they tend livestock, and they have brought along their flocks and herds and everything they own."'" — Gen 46:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph does not just bring his family to Egypt and hope for the best. He thinks it through. He plans what he will say to Pharaoh, decides what to emphasise, and briefs his family beforehand.

He is being wise. His family are simple shepherds arriving in the most sophisticated empire on earth, and Joseph is managing their arrival carefully so that they land well.

Faith and planning are not opposites. Some Christians treat careful preparation as though it shows a lack of trust in God. Scripture does not agree. The book of Proverbs is full of praise for planning, and Jesus Himself spoke about counting the cost before you build (Lk 14:28).

The difference is where our confidence sits. Jacob worshipped at Beersheba before he set out; Joseph plans thoroughly in Goshen. Both are right. We commit our way to the Lord and then we use the sense He gave us.

Notice also what Joseph is not doing: he is not asking his family to pretend to be something they are not. He plans to tell Pharaoh plainly that they are shepherds. Wisdom, not dishonesty.

Pray, then think. Trust God, then prepare.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat planning and trusting God as opposites?
2. Where do you need to think more carefully rather than just hoping it works out?
3. Where might your "planning" actually be anxiety in disguise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to trust You fully and to use the wisdom You have given me. Show me the difference between careful planning and anxious control. Amen.
